results.title: What are managed agents? | Google Cloud
results.content:
## How does Google support managed agents?

Managed Agents in the Gemini API provides a managed environment for building agents that can work through complex, multi-step tasks.

Instead of requiring developers to build the complete environment around an agent themselves, Managed Agents can provide an isolated workspace where an agent can reason about a goal, execute code, work with files, and use tools as it progresses through a task. Developers can customize the agent with their own instructions and connect it to the tools and information their application needs. [...] This creates a different abstraction from a standard model API call. With a model API, the developer sends input to a model and receives an output. With a managed agent, the developer can provide a goal and give the agent an environment where it can take multiple actions to accomplish it.

## Get started with managed AI agents

Developers can experiment with managed AI agents using several different Google offerings:

 Gemini platform [...] Gemini platform

  Deploy autonomous AI agents such as the config-driven Managed Agents API to automate complex enterprise tasks without managing the underlying infrastructure. Each managed agent operates within a secure, isolated sandbox container where it autonomously reasons, executes code, searches the web, and connects to enterprise tools and data sources.
 Google AI Studio

  Serves as the visual playground and prototyping console for developers building on the Gemini API. It includes a dedicated "Agents" tab to experiment with managed agent templates (like the general-purpose Antigravity Agent) without writing any code.
 Managed Agents in the Gemini API

### Human oversight

Agents can reason, plan, and execute multi-step workflows with a high degree of autonomy. While this is powerful, it also means you should apply appropriate oversight—particularly for tasks that modify data or interact with external systems.

Always verify critical outputs—such as generated code, data transformations, or configuration changes—before deploying them.

## Support and feedback

Email the public discussion group at `managed-agents-in-agent-platform@google.com` for support and feedback on Managed Agents API on Agent Platform.

results.title: Claude Managed Agents
results.content:
Interchangeable, disposable execution environments.

If a container fails, the harness treats it as a tool-call error and passes that feedback to Claude.

New containers spin up without manual intervention.

This decoupled architecture delivers real performance gains.

Source

### How It works step by step

Working with Managed Agents follows a clear four-step flow:

#### Step 1: Create an Agent

Define what the agent is … its model, system prompt, and available tools.

This is a one-time setup that you reference by ID.

```
from anthropic import Anthropic client = Anthropic() agent = client.beta.agents.create( name=”Coding Assistant”, model=”claude-sonnet-4-6”, system=”You are a helpful coding assistant.”, tools=[{”type”: “agent_toolset_20260401”}], )
```
